children: finance leader exits after roles spanning pipelines, business development and new energy ventures

Gagandeep Singh Kohli, Executive Director (Finance), Pipelines and Business Development at IndianOil, has retired after more than three decades with the company. During his career, Kohli held finance leadership responsibilities across hydrocarbons, LNG, compressed biogas and green energy, while also supporting domestic and international business ventures.

Kohli’s career at IndianOil covered finance functions across marketing, pipelines and business development. His responsibilities included financial management, corporate governance, business planning and strategic support for the company’s operations and investments.
In his most recent role as Executive Director (Finance), Pipelines and Business Development, he provided financial leadership across a portfolio of domestic and international ventures.
Kohli was associated with businesses and ventures including IndianOil LNG, IndianOil GPS Renewables and IndianOil Montney Canada.

His finance responsibilities extended across conventional hydrocarbons as well as newer areas of the energy business. He was involved in supporting IndianOil’s activities in LNG, compressed biogas and green energy as the company expanded its presence across these segments.
His international exposure also included work related to IndianOil’s operations and investments outside India.

Kohli’s tenure also included a focus on digital finance transformation. His work brought together financial management and technology-led changes in finance processes across a large energy organisation.
His roles involved supporting business decisions through financial analysis, governance and controls while working with teams across different business verticals.

Beyond finance responsibilities, Kohli’s career included a focus on team development and professional mentorship. His leadership experience covered financial governance, business development and strategic planning across multiple energy segments.

His retirement marks the end of a career spanning more than three decades at IndianOil, during which the company’s business expanded into LNG, renewable energy and other emerging areas alongside its established hydrocarbon operations.

Kohli’s career reflects the widening role of finance leadership in the energy sector, with finance functions increasingly linked to investment decisions, business transformation, governance and new energy opportunities.
